quotes.text: Mesh is not a virtual world you live in. It's a meeting space you enter for specific sessions. No persistent universe, no digital real estate to buy
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the most common misconception about Mesh as a metaverse.

quotes.text: Companies didn't want another platform to manage, since they already have Teams and Microsoft 365. They didn't want to learn a whole new tool just for a 3D meeting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why Microsoft folded Mesh into Teams.

quotes.text: Side conversations become possible again. In a regular Teams call, if two people want to chat privately, they have to send a separate message or leave the meeting entirely. In an immersive space, they just step aside.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows the concrete benefit of spatial audio over a normal video call.

quotes.text: The most successful use cases involve interaction, not passive watching. Mesh works best when people need to move, talk and collaborate.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear rule of thumb for when immersive meetings add value.

takeaways: Microsoft Mesh is no longer a standalone metaverse platform; it lives on as immersive 3D spaces inside Microsoft Teams meetings.
Avatars and spatial audio create a sense of presence and make side conversations possible, which reduces meeting fatigue.
Immersive spaces are capped at 16 people with no custom worlds, so they fit interactive team meetings, onboarding and training rather than webinars.
hook: Microsoft Mesh is surrounded by metaverse buzzwords, yet few people can explain what it does today. This Simply Explained episode is for Teams users and IT decision makers who want to know how Mesh became immersive spaces in Teams, how avatars and spatial audio work, and when a 3D meeting actually beats a video call.
